title: Agentic AI: 5-Week Weekly Learning Plan
weekly_structure: Days 1–6 cover concepts and implementation; day 7 is for integration, tests, review, and catch-up.

weeks.name: Raw LLM and Function Calling
weeks.goal: Build a bounded tool-using agent in raw Python before using orchestration frameworks.
weeks.project_scope: A CLI assistant with workspace-scoped read_file and write_file tools plus a fixed allowlisted test command. It observes test output and may attempt bounded repairs.
definition_of_done: The assistant can call approved tools and use their results.
All tool inputs are validated.
The loop has iteration/time limits.
File tools are confined to a dedicated workspace and commands are allowlisted.

weeks.name: Agentic RAG and Memory
weeks.goal: Give an agent controlled access to a knowledge base and persistent, user-scoped memory.
key_topics: CRAG-inspired relevance grading and query rewriting
weeks.project_scope: A document research agent that retrieves chunks, checks relevance, rewrites a query within a retry limit, optionally falls back to an external search adapter, cites sources, and stores explicitly selected memories.
week_end_evidence: User-scoped memory CRUD and retention policy
definition_of_done: Answers expose source references.
Insufficient evidence results in abstention or an explicit fallback.
Retrieval retries are bounded.
Persistent memories are user-scoped, inspectable, and deletable.

weeks.name: LangGraph, MCP, and Multi-Agent Systems
weeks.goal: Represent complex agent execution as a stateful graph and connect tools through MCP.
weeks.project_scope: A supervisor coordinates researcher, fact-checker, and writer roles. Research and verification capabilities are exposed through a local MCP server/client integration.
definition_of_done: The graph has explicit state and bounded cycles.
A workflow can resume from a checkpoint.
The MCP client can discover and call an approved server tool.
Specialist responsibilities and handoffs are explicit.

weeks.name: Human-in-the-Loop, Guardrails, and Reliability
weeks.goal: Make the agent controlled, auditable, resilient to failures, and resistant to unsafe tool requests.
weeks.project_scope: An extension of P3 that adds a mock publishing action, server-side permission checks, approval interrupts, bounded retries, idempotency, audit records, and adversarial tests.
definition_of_done: No publish action can run without a valid approval.
Tool authorization is enforced in application code.
Duplicate side effects are prevented on retry.
Prompt-injection, failure, and rejection scenarios are tested.

weeks.name: Deployment, Tracing, and AgentOps
weeks.goal: Deliver the guarded workflow through a documented, observable, containerized backend service.
key_topics: Tracing with Langfuse or Arize Phoenix
weeks.weekly_project_name: Production-Oriented Agentic Research and Publishing API
weeks.project_scope: A FastAPI service that runs the P4 workflow, persists state, streams safe progress events, exposes approval/status endpoints, records traces, and is packaged in Docker. Publishing remains mocked or explicitly controlled unless a real integration is separately authorized.
definition_of_done: The service can be started from a clean setup using the README.
Runs and checkpoints survive restart.
Progress events do not expose hidden chain-of-thought or secrets.
Approval and authorization controls remain enforced.
The final demo includes measured evaluation results and clear limitations.
